For the full year, we achieved an operating ratio of 66.4%, and an adjusted operating ratio of 65.8% (see our non-GAAP reconciliations beginning on page K26), both of which improved on a year-over-year basis. We remain committed to being a safe, productive, resilient, and efficient railroad with industry-competitive margins.

## Norfolk Southern Corp (CIK 702165) — Profitability margin change, FY2024 vs FY2023

**Period used:** fiscal years ended 2024-12-31 and 2023-12-31 (both 10-K, FY, full-year flows; 2023 comparatives taken from the FY2024 10-K, accession 0000702165-25-000008, which matches the FY2023 10-K, accession 0000702165-24-000005).

### Margins (all derived by me from disclosed USD amounts; revenue = `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax`)

| Metric | 2023 | 2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Railway operating revenues | $12,156M (fact 859726/859727) | $12,123M (fact 859736) | −0.3% |
| Income from railway operations | $2,851M (fact 855249/855250) | $4,071M (fact 855259) | +42.8% |
| Pre-tax income | $2,320M (fact 850744/850745) | $3,329M (fact 850754) | +43.5% |
| Net income | $1,827M (fact 854468/854469) | $2,622M (fact 854482) | +43.5% |
| **Operating margin** | 23.5% | 33.6% | **+10.1 pts** |
| **Pre-tax margin** | 19.1% | 27.5% | **+8.4 pts** |
| **Net margin** | 15.0% | 21.6% | **+6.6 pts** |
| Operating ratio (expenses/revenue) | 76.5% (reported) | 66.4% (reported) | −10.1 pts |

The company's own disclosed railway operating ratio was 76.5% in 2023 and 66.4% in 2024 (adjusted 65.8%), a 9.1-point improvement (report chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:9989 and :88217).

### What drove the change
Revenue was essentially flat (−$33M), so the entire margin gain came from the expense side: total costs and expenses fell from $9,305M to $8,052M (−$1,253M, −13.5%) (facts 847164/847165 → 847174).

Per the FY2024 MD&A (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:84561, :102870, :89477):
1. **Lower net Eastern Ohio (derailment) incident costs** — 2023 included ~$1.1 billion of environmental and legal charges; 2024 had much lower net incident expense. This is the single largest driver.
2. **$433 million of gains on sales of railway lines** (plus other higher gains on operating property sales), which reduced reported operating expenses.
3. **Lower fuel prices** — fuel expense fell from $1,170M to $987M (facts 850437/850438 → 850447); locomotive fuel prices were down 15%, cutting fuel expense by $159M, with gallons roughly flat (373M vs 377M).
4. **Lower purchased-services costs and lower other expenses**, plus operational improvements that let the railroad handle 5% higher volumes.
5. **Partially offsetting:** restructuring and other charges, and higher depreciation ($1,298M → $1,353M; facts 848643/848644 → 848650) on a larger asset base. Labor and related expense was essentially flat ($2,819M → $2,823M; facts 852602/852603 → 852612).

### Why net margin rose less than operating margin
Below the operating line, the improvement was diluted: other income–net dropped from $191M to $65M (facts 857204/857205 → 857214) and interest expense rose from $722M to $807M (facts 852178/852179 → 852181). The effective tax rate was essentially unchanged (21.3% → 21.2%; facts 849527/849528 → 849530), so taxes did not drive the difference. Hence net margin gained 6.6 points versus 10.1 points at the operating line.

### Limitations
- Margins and the operating ratio are my calculations from disclosed XBRL values, not directly reported fields; the company's own reported operating ratio (66.4%/76.5%) is quoted separately.
- A meaningful part of the 2024 improvement is non-recurring in nature (incident-cost comparison and $433M of line-sale gains), so the reported margin expansion overstates the underlying recurring improvement; the company's adjusted operating ratio of 65.8% still excludes these items.
- The database does not expose a clean "purchased services" or "other expenses" tag for both years, so those components are supported by MD&A narrative rather than by matched XBRL line items.

The company's own disclosed railway operating ratio was 76.5% in 2023 and 66.4% in 2024 (adjusted 65.8%), a 9.1-point improvement (report chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:9989 and :88217).

### What drove the change
Revenue was essentially flat (−$33M), so the entire margin gain came from the expense side: total costs and expenses fell from $9,305M to $8,052M (−$1,253M, −13.5%) (facts 847164/847165 → 847174).

Per the FY2024 MD&A (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:84561, :102870, :89477):
1. **Lower net Eastern Ohio (derailment) incident costs** — 2023 included ~$1.1 billion of environmental and legal charges; 2024 had much lower net incident expense. This is the single largest driver.
2. **$433 million of gains on sales of railway lines** (plus other higher gains on operating property sales), which reduced reported operating expenses.
3. **Lower fuel prices** — fuel expense fell from $1,170M to $987M (facts 850437/850438 → 850447); locomotive fuel prices were down 15%, cutting fuel expense by $159M, with gallons roughly flat (373M vs 377M).
4. **Lower purchased-services costs and lower other expenses**, plus operational improvements that let the railroad handle 5% higher volumes.
5. **Partially offsetting:** restructuring and other charges, and higher depreciation ($1,298M → $1,353M; facts 848643/848644 → 848650) on a larger asset base. Labor and related expense was essentially flat ($2,819M → $2,823M; facts 852602/852603 → 852612).

### Why net margin rose less than operating margin
Below the operating line, the improvement was diluted: other income–net dropped from $191M to $65M (facts 857204/857205 → 857214) and interest expense rose from $722M to $807M (facts 852178/852179 → 852181). The effective tax rate was essentially unchanged (21.3% → 21.2%; facts 849527/849528 → 849530), so taxes did not drive the difference. Hence net margin gained 6.6 points versus 10.1 points at the operating line.

### Limitations
- Margins and the operating ratio are my calculations from disclosed XBRL values, not directly reported fields; the company's own reported operating ratio (66.4%/76.5%) is quoted separately.
- A meaningful part of the 2024 improvement is non-recurring in nature (incident-cost comparison and $433M of line-sale gains), so the reported margin expansion overstates the underlying recurring improvement; the company's adjusted operating ratio of 65.8% still excludes these items.
- The database does not expose a clean "purchased services" or "other expenses" tag for both years, so those components are supported by MD&A narrative rather than by matched XBRL line items.
